To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
KDM4b promotes resistance to next‐ generation antiandrogens through AR‐dependent upregulation of c‐Mycin prostate cancer.
KDM4 is overexpressed and regulates the sensitivity to anti‐androgen therapy through AR‐mediated MYC expression.
KDM4b is a novel androgen receptor co‐activator that regulates sensitivity to androgen deprivation therapy and next‐generation antiandrogens through epigenetic regulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel mechanism of action (MOA) for a novel class of small molecule inhibitors.
the role of the KDM4‐AR‐c‐Myc signaling axis in prostate cancer progression and resistance to anti‐androgen treatment.
the development of a new approach to the development of a wide range of cancer patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the authors found that overexpression of KDM 4B promoted recruitment to the c-Myc gene enhancer and enhanced AR-dependent transcription of c-Myc mRNA, which regulated the sensitivity to AR targeted therapy.

“Our results revealed a novel AR–KDM4B–c‐MYC axis in advanced prostate cancer which could be targeted by inhibition of KDM 4B to reduce c‐MYC expression and overcome resistance of AR‐targeted treatments”.

this paper is a nice piece of work that adds to our current understanding of how the KDM4‐B protein can regulate androgen receptor‐mediated transcription of c‐MYC and how this can be targeted therapeutically in advanced prostate cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the histone demethylases KDM4B and KDM5B are upregulated in advanced prostate cancer, and they promote AR‐dependent transcriptional regulation of c‐Myl mRNA, which confers resistance to anti‐androgents and AR‐targeted inhibitors.
the KDM4‐AR‐c‐Myc pathway plays an important role in the progression of prostate cancer and resistance to AR‐directed therapy.
KDM4b plays an essential role in the development of enzalutamid resistance by upregulating c‐Myc, which could be targeted by KDM4b inhibition to overcome resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
KDM4b is a potential therapeutic target to overcome anti‐androgen therapy resistance in prostate cancer.
KDM4b is an important co‐activator of AR, and it is required for prostate cancer progression and for resistance to next‐ generation AR‐targeted drugs, including enzalutamid.

we have discovered a novel mechanism of resistance to next‐ generation anti‐androgene therapy, and that inhibition of the KDM4‐AR–c‐MYC pathway can overcome resistance to next‐generations anti‐androgans.
